doc.title: Byron Stripling interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 25, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Covid as a gift that exposes ignored problems
summary: He sees the pandemic as a gift wrapped in a problem that exposed healthcare gaps and racism, linking it to protests.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: All right. Do you have any feeling about why in 2020, or this time in our history, that this pandemic occurred?

Yes. Because God, if you believe in God, whatever you believe, if God wants to give you a gift he wraps it in a problem. And so I think we’ve been given a gift and we’ve been made to look at ourselves and look at our actions, and we can either see and learn the lessons from those, but we’ve had problems all this whole time that we’ve ignored. And there’s a saying that says that problem that you have is now two, is now three, because you ignored it, now four because you ignored it. And it begins to grow exponentially. And that’s like with the protests and things that we have, because Covid obviously has not only exposed bare our weaknesses in healthcare, I mean it makes no sense that people could get sick and lose their job and then have the burden to worry if they could pay to get themselves well. Screw GoFundMe. Why should you have to raise money so you can breathe, right? So this is what we’re dealing with. So we’ve ignored these problems, and problems always come back to you. So now we’ve been given this gift that pulled the covers off of the whole thing. It pulled it off racism, because people had a chance to sort of bathe in it and then we had a president that stoked it and lit a fire and threw flames and stuff on it, and so the expectation is you’re just going to sit there? No we’re going to go out and do what we’ve always done, we’re going to protest and let people know what these feelings are. And then people will try to misconstrue what you’re thinking and how you’re doing, what you’re doing. And they’ll make lies up about you and the guy goes and kneels because he wants to protest police violence. And you say, “You’re just an athlete” and then what’s the great basketball player, LeBron James, makes a statement and they tell him, “Shut up and dribble. Shut up and dribble. Dribble.” Right?
